title: Cuba’s Point of No Return
gist: Will Freeman argues Cuba has reached a point of no return where the country is physically and economically collapsing even as its regime survives, illustrated by the unrepaired collapse of a historic Havana building. Only the opening of the paywalled essay is available.

insights.claim: Cuba as a country is collapsing even as its communist regime survives, decoupling state failure from regime change.
insights.speaker: Will Freeman
insights.so_what: Do not assume economic collapse in Cuba triggers political transition; regime-change-driven opening trades (tourism, remittances, real estate) remain speculative.
insights.quote: The Country Is Collapsing Even as Its Regime Survives

insights.claim: The 166-year-old building of Havana's Superior Institute of Industrial Design suffered two partial collapses in 2025 that the state never repaired, then fell completely in February 2026, entombing several squatters.
insights.speaker: Will Freeman
insights.so_what: Illustrates the Cuban state's inability to maintain basic infrastructure, a proxy for fiscal exhaustion.
insights.quote: The state never sent anyone to fix it.
insights.locator: In central Havana, a giant mound

insights.claim: By June 2026, men were scavenging bricks from the rubble of the collapsed Havana building, pointing to acute material scarcity and an informal survival economy.
insights.speaker: Will Freeman
insights.so_what: Signals deep scarcity of basic materials; any recovery would require large external capital inflows.
